literal: When the King reached Ye, he executed Yang, Yan, and the others.
idiomatic: When the King reached Ye, he put Yang, Yan, and their faction to death.

literal: An edict appointed him Grand Chancellor and Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, with authority over civil and military affairs, and he returned to Bingzhou.
idiomatic: An edict made him Grand Chancellor and supreme commander of all forces, civil and military, and he went back to Bingzhou.

literal: When he arrived, Yan Xi said to him: "Had you taken my counsel earlier, those petty men would not have seized power and we would nearly have been overthrown.
idiomatic: On his arrival Yan Xi said, "Had you heeded me sooner, petty men would never have held the reins and we would almost have been ruined.

literal: Those beside the throne are cleared for the moment—but in the end how will you deal with me?"
idiomatic: The court is clean for now—but what will you do with me in the end?"

literal: Xi replied: "Your Highness's former standing still allowed you to take office or leave it under the teaching of moral names.
idiomatic: Xi answered, "Your Highness's old rank still let you enter or leave office by the norms of moral teaching.

literal: Today's situation turns on Heaven's timing; it is no longer within what human reason can reach."
idiomatic: Today's turn of affairs hangs on Heaven's hour; it is past what men can argue."

literal: Before long it was memorialized to appoint Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui as Left Chief Steward; Xi was made Administrator.
idiomatic: Soon a memorial named Prince Rui of Zhao commandery Left Chief Steward and made Xi his Administrator.

literal: Each night he was brought in by carriage; by day they did not speak with him, because Xi was scholarly and slow and they feared he would not satisfy the military men's wishes.
idiomatic: He was carted in every night yet not spoken to by day—Xi was too bookish and mild to please the generals.

literal: Later the King entered Xi's private room and said: "Lately the nobles press me hard, saying I go against Heaven and court ill fortune, and I fear some uprising may come; I mean to bind them by the proper law."
idiomatic: Later the King came to Xi's chamber and said, "The great families hound me, calling my course unlucky and heaven-defying. I fear trouble and mean to punish them by law."

literal: Xi said: "The court of late has kept kin at a distance and scarcely remembers the weight of flesh and bone.
idiomatic: Xi said, "The court has lately estranged its kin and forgotten the weight of blood."

literal: What Your Highness has done in haste is no longer the conduct of a subject.
idiomatic: What you have done in haste is no longer how a subject should act.

literal: A thorn in the back, crossed halberds at the throat—superior and inferior doubting each other—how can that long endure?
idiomatic: Dagger at your back, blades at your neck—ruler and ruled doubting one another—how can that last?

literal: Moreover Heaven's way is not constant; loss and gain take turns; divine calculation shifts, and omens gather.
idiomatic: Heaven's way is not fixed; waxing and waning alternate; omens shift and spirits stir.

literal: Though you hold humility in check, you treat the sacred vessel as chaff.
idiomatic: Though you feign humility, you treat the throne as chaff.

literal: That is to go against the Supreme Mystery and topple your forefathers' foundation."
idiomatic: That defies Heaven above and casts down your fathers' house."

literal: The King said: "How dare you speak what your beard should not say!
idiomatic: The King cried, "How dare you say what no beard should utter!

literal: I must bring you to law."
idiomatic: I will have you punished by law."

literal: Xi said: "I take it that Heaven's timing and human affairs follow one measure.
idiomatic: Xi said, "Heaven's hour and men's affairs, I believe, share one rule.

literal: Therefore I offend the thunderbolt and do not fear axe and halberd.
idiomatic: So I brave the thunderbolt and do not fear the axe.

literal: Today I may lay bare liver and gall; perhaps the spirits too approve."
idiomatic: Today I lay my heart bare—and perhaps the spirits approve."

literal: The King said: "To rescue peril and set the age right still awaits a sage; how dare I debate in private? Pray speak no more."
idiomatic: The King said, "To save the age still wants a sage—how dare I plot in private? Say no more."

literal: Soon an edict came: because the Chancellor's burden was heavy, all staff in his bureau were promoted one grade; Xi as Administrator also held the post of Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: Soon an edict, citing the Chancellor's heavy load, raised every man in his bureau one grade; Xi as Administrator also headed a personnel desk.

literal: Lu Yao, Attendant Gentleman in the Chancellor's service, was about to go on a mission; at parting he grasped Xi's hand and said: "The Chancellor's merit fills the realm; the world gladly pushes him forward; songs fill the roads and nothing else is desired.
idiomatic: Lu Yao of the Chancellor's staff was leaving on a mission; at farewell he seized Xi's hand. "The Chancellor's merit fills the realm; all men push him forward; songs crowd the roads and every heart looks one way.

literal: We lie prostrate and wish to lay bare our loyal hearts.
idiomatic: We lie prostrate and would bare our hearts.

literal: Yet suddenly I am sent abroad and cannot speak my short plea face to face; my inch of heart I respectfully raise to you."
idiomatic: Yet I am sent away and cannot speak face to face; this inch of heart I raise to you."

literal: Xi soon repeated Yao's words.
idiomatic: Xi soon repeated Yao's words to the King.

literal: The King said: "If inside and outside alike harbor such hopes, Zhao Yanshen is at my side morning and night—why has he never said a word?
idiomatic: The King said, "If court and camp share this wish, Zhao Yanshen is with me day and night—why has he never spoken?

literal: Try in secret what you think and speak with him."
idiomatic: Sound him out in secret as you think best."

literal: Xi took an opening to ask Yanshen.
idiomatic: Xi found a moment to ask Yanshen.

literal: He said: "I too have been startled by these songs; each time I wished to report it my mouth froze and my heart trembled.
idiomatic: Yanshen said, "These songs startled me too; each time I meant to speak my mouth froze and my heart shook.

literal: Since you have broached the matter, I too will risk death and lay bare liver and gall once."
idiomatic: Now that you have opened the matter, I too will risk death and lay my heart bare."

literal: He likewise urged the same course.
idiomatic: He urged the same course as the others.

literal: At that time the kings, dukes, ministers, and generals daily pressed the plea; governors and prefects from the four quarters tabled memorials with portents of mandate.
idiomatic: Kings, dukes, ministers, and generals pressed daily; governors from the four quarters tabled portents of the mandate.

literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Qianming, Emperor Zhao ascended the throne.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of Qianming 1, Emperor Zhao took the throne.

literal: In the ninth month Xi was made Regular Attendant and continued to hold the concurrent post of Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Xi was made Regular Attendant and still held his personnel post.

literal: Later, when a memorial audience ended, the Emperor said at ease: "Lately why have you made yourself like an outsider I can scarcely see?
idiomatic: After an audience the Emperor said gently, "Why lately do you act like a stranger I can hardly see?

literal: From now on, unless it is your bureau's business, whenever you have something in mind write a note as you please and, when a brief gap appears, bring it straight in."
idiomatic: Henceforth, unless it is bureau business, write whatever is on your mind and bring it in the first spare moment."

literal: He therefore ordered Yang Xiuzhi of the Ministry of Personnel, Cui Li of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, and two others—three men in all—each day when their regular duties ended to enter together the east corridor.
idiomatic: He ordered Yang Xiuzhi, Cui Li, and one other—three men—to join the east corridor after daily duties.

literal: Together they were to record rites and music abandoned through the ages, offices abolished, differences in court sacrifice, changes in carriage and dress, or men of lofty virtue long sunk in obscurity, or clever words that dazzle the vulgar and evil that harms government, reaching to markets, taxes, marriage and burial, noble and base—whatever was inconvenient to the times yet still used from past to present, or useful in antiquity yet cast away today—and think through all in detail and report item by item.
idiomatic: Together they were to catalogue lost rites and music, abolished offices, changes in sacrifice and dress, worthy men long buried in obscurity, flashy words and harmful cults, markets, taxes, marriage and burial, rank and mean—whatever ill fit the age yet lingered, or what antiquity used and today threw away—and report step by step.

literal: They need not wait until all was ready; whenever something came to mind they might continue to report.
idiomatic: They need not finish all at once; whenever memory stirred they could report again.

literal: Morning and evening they were given imperial pantry food; at day's end they were dismissed.
idiomatic: Morning and evening they ate from the imperial pantry; at dusk they went home.

literal: When the hundred officials asked to establish an Eastern Palace, the edict was not granted; each time Xi was sent to the east hall to oversee the crown prince's cap and robes and guide his steps in obeisance.
idiomatic: When officials asked for an Heir Apparent's establishment, the throne refused; Xi was sent to the east hall to watch the crown prince's dress and guide his bows.

literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

literal: Xi in his bureau duty presented the seal to the crown prince.
idiomatic: In bureau duty Xi presented the seal to the crown prince.

literal: At the crown prince's sacrifice to the sage he also served as Junior Mentor.
idiomatic: At the crown prince's school sacrifice he also served as Junior Mentor.

literal: The Emperor said to him: "Now that you hold heavy office, you must not be at ease and slack as before."
idiomatic: The Emperor told him, "Now that your post is weighty, you must not lounge as before."

literal: When the Emperor was about to campaign north he ordered and asked: "What have you heard lately?"
idiomatic: Before a northern campaign the Emperor asked, "What have you heard lately?"

literal: Xi said: "On the roads they say the imperial carriage will set out."
idiomatic: Xi said, "The roads say the carriage will march."

literal: The Emperor said: "The Kumo Xi raid the south; I have not yet led troops myself and therefore wish a little to drill in arms."
idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The Kumo Xi raid south; I have never led an army and wish to learn war on the march."

literal: Xi said: "The imperial carriage on tour—what is the need?
idiomatic: Xi said, "The sacred carriage on tour—to what end?

literal: If you lightly take the field, I fear the realm will lose heart."
idiomatic: If you lightly go to war, the realm will lose heart."

literal: The Emperor said: "That is the coward's constant worry; I myself will weigh matters when the time comes."
idiomatic: The Emperor said, "That is a coward's fret; I will judge when the hour comes."

literal: The Emperor sent the fast-officer Pei Ze and the chief clerk Cai Hui to spy on the court below, fond of false accusations; courtiers called them Pei and Cai.
idiomatic: He sent Pei Ze and Cai Hui to spy on officials, given to slander; men called them Pei and Cai.

literal: At that time the two reported: "After the northern campaign Yang Xiuzhi and Wang Xi several times feasted and roamed with others and did not keep public business in mind."
idiomatic: They reported, "After the northern march Yang Xiuzhi and Wang Xi feasted and wandered and neglected office."

literal: The Emperor had Xiuzhi and Xi flogged forty strokes on the shins.
idiomatic: The Emperor had both men flogged forty strokes on the shins.

literal: The Emperor executed a man before him and asked Xi: "Does this man deserve death?"
idiomatic: He beheaded a man before Xi and asked, "Did this man deserve death?"

literal: Xi said: "His crime indeed deserved death, but I regret that he did not die in the proper place.
idiomatic: Xi said, "His crime deserved death, but not here.

literal: I have heard that punishment is carried out in the market and the multitude casts the body away;
idiomatic: I have heard punishment belongs in the market, where the people cast the body away;

literal: the palace hall is not a place for killing."
idiomatic: the palace is no place to kill."

literal: The Emperor changed expression and said: "From now on I shall change this for the kings and dukes."
idiomatic: The Emperor's face changed. "From now on I shall change this—for kings and dukes alike."

literal: The Emperor wished to make Xi Attendant-in-Ordinary; he firmly declined and would not accept.
idiomatic: The Emperor wished to make him Attendant-in-Ordinary; Xi firmly refused.

literal: Some urged Xi not to distance himself; Xi said: "From my youth I have seen many men in high favor.
idiomatic: Some urged him not to stand apart; Xi said, "Since youth I have watched many favorites.

literal: Filled to satiety in their brief hour, few did not end in ruin.
idiomatic: Sated for a moment, few escaped ruin.

literal: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow; I cannot bear the affairs of the time.
idiomatic: My nature is loose and slow; I cannot bear the times.

literal: A ruler's private favor—how can it be kept?
idiomatic: A ruler's private grace—how can it be kept?

literal: If by chance things turn wild, there will be nowhere to seek recall.
idiomatic: If fortune turns, there is nowhere to flee.

literal: It is not that I do not love a hot office; I have only thought it through to the core."
idiomatic: I do not dislike a glittering post; I have only chewed the thought to the bone."

literal: When the hundred officials were granted an archery contest, Xi hit the target and should have received silk, but because he did not mark his arrow the office would not give it.
idiomatic: At an archery grant Xi hit the mark and should have won silk, but he did not mark his arrow and the office refused payment.

literal: Xi said cheerfully: "This time I may be called strong in war and weak in letters."
idiomatic: Xi laughed, "This time I may be called war-strong and letter-weak."

literal: Xi had no son; the Emperor was about to give him a concubine.
idiomatic: Xi had no son; the Emperor meant to give him a concubine.

literal: He sent a junior yellow gate to his house to proclaim the intent; the empress sent word to Xi's wife.
idiomatic: A junior eunuch proclaimed the intent at his house; the empress sent word to his wife.

literal: Xi had his wife answer; his wife never spoke; Xi brushed his chest with his hand and withdrew.
idiomatic: Xi had his wife answer; she said nothing; Xi touched his chest and withdrew.

literal: When the Emperor heard it he laughed.
idiomatic: The Emperor laughed when he heard.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, Xi's grief was such that he nearly could not survive; because of this he fell into emaciation and decline.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, Xi grieved until he nearly perished and wasted away.

literal: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his scholarly slowness and therefore disliked him all the more.
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his bookish slowness and disliked him the more.

literal: When he reported on business he was greatly berated, yet he walked at ease with his elegant step.
idiomatic: Reporting to court he was savagely scolded, yet walked at ease with his elegant step.

literal: He served as Inspector of East Xuzhou and Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He served as Inspector of East Xuzhou and Director of the Secretariat.

literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was moved to Grand Herald, with the added title Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, supervised the drafting of the imperial diary, and attended at the Forest of Literature.
idiomatic: At the start of Wuping he became Grand Herald with honors equal to the Three Dukes, supervised the imperial diary, and attended at the Forest of Literature.

literal: His nature was leisurely and he desired little; though kingly business pressed thick, his refined conduct did not shift.
idiomatic: He was leisurely and desired little; though royal business pressed thick, his refined conduct never shifted.

literal: In Bingzhou, though war-horses filled the lanes, he never took worldly affairs as a burden.
idiomatic: In Bingzhou, though war-horses filled the lanes, he never let the world weigh on him.

literal: On fine days and fair scenes he would chant and roam, climb hills and waters, and make talk and feasting his business; gentlemen called him "the Grand Administrator beyond the world."
idiomatic: On fair days he chanted and roamed, climbed hills and streams, and made feasting his trade; men called him the Grand Administrator beyond the world.

literal: Visiting the Jin Shrine he composed a poem: "The sun sets—I should return; fish and birds seem to detain me."
idiomatic: At the Jin Shrine he wrote, "The sun sets and I should go home; fish and birds seem to hold me back."

literal: Suddenly a messenger of the King summoned him; Xi did not come at once.
idiomatic: Suddenly the King's messenger called; Xi did not come at once.

literal: The next day Lu Sidao, Libationer of the Chancellor's western pavilion, said to Xi: "Yesterday's summons already flushed your face—can fish and birds have brought blame?"
idiomatic: Next day Lu Sidao said, "Yesterday's summons flushed you red—did fish and birds bring the blame?"

literal: Xi smiled slowly: "Last night I was merry and was rather fined in wine.
idiomatic: Xi smiled, "Last night I was merry and was fined in wine.

literal: You fellows too are things that detain one—not only fish and birds."
idiomatic: You too are things that detain—not only fish and birds."

literal: When Jinyang fell in defeat he fled northeast with like-minded men to escape Zhou troops.
idiomatic: When Jinyang fell he fled northeast with friends to escape Zhou troops.

literal: The mountain road was perilous and steep; they feared bandits, yet Xi warmed wine and took unguent and never once stopped.
idiomatic: The mountain road was steep and bandits feared, yet Xi warmed wine and took salve and never once stopped.

literal: Each time he would not hurry away and his companions especially blamed him.
idiomatic: He would not hurry and his companions blamed him.

literal: Xi said: "Do not blame me—if I acted without regret I would long since have been one of the Three Dukes."
idiomatic: Xi said, "Blame me not—had I never regretted my way I would long since have been a Three Duke."

literal: Hao, styled Jigao, from youth established name and conduct and was praised by scholar-friends.
idiomatic: Hao, styled Jigao, won name and conduct early and was praised by friends.

literal: When his mother died he mourned with utmost filial feeling.
idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned with utmost filial feeling.

literal: His scholarly slowness was the same as his elder brothers'.
idiomatic: His scholarly slowness matched his brothers'.

literal: Once he followed Emperor Wenxuan on a northern campaign, riding a red horse; at dawn it was covered with frost and he could no longer recognize it.
idiomatic: Once on Emperor Wenxuan's northern campaign he rode a red horse; at dawn frost covered it and he did not know it.

literal: He said he had lost his horse; the camp guards searched but could not find it.
idiomatic: He said his horse was lost; guards searched in vain.

literal: In a moment the sun rose, the frost on the horse's body melted away, and it was tied before the tent; then he said: "My horse is still here."
idiomatic: The sun rose, the frost melted, and the horse stood before the tent; he said, "My horse is still here."

literal: As a clerk in the Secretariat he listened for the noon drum at court, pacing in small steps waiting to leave.
idiomatic: As Secretariat clerk he listened for the noon drum, pacing small steps to leave.

literal: The assembled clerks mocked him: "Wang the Seventh, why such haste to go home?"
idiomatic: Clerks mocked him, "Wang the Seventh, why such haste home?"

literal: Jigao said: "The great peng is just about to rise—why do swallows and sparrows chirp so?"
idiomatic: Jigao said, "The great peng is about to rise—why do sparrows chirp?"

literal: The mockers said: "Whose house is dead ahead—the door-boss roams in idle sport."
idiomatic: The mockers said, "Whose house stands ahead—the door-knob roams in idle sport."
